messages:
ergon_customer: hey, we started getting a bunch of 422s from /v1/generate when using json_mode=strict. no code changes on our side. happening in us-west and eu-central. repro below.

ergon_customer: repro curl (redacted token):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \n  -H "Accept: application/json" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"summarize: ...","response_format":"json","json_mode":"strict"}'
```

ergon_customer: response we see is 422 with an HTML body (looks like an upstream error page). request_id=0a9f5d2c. saw it first at 2170001111 and repeated until 2170001205.

alice_support: thanks — can you confirm you include Accept: application/json on every request and that the token is valid? also can you paste any proxy/cdn in front of your clients?

ergon_customer: confirm Accept present always. no auth rotate. we do have a CDN in front that might add Vary headers.

carla_sre: pulled the trace for 0a9f5d2c — upstream service returned 500 with Content-Type: text/html during a transient maintenance window. our strict-json path sees non-json content-type and maps it to 422 (invalid_json) which is how you saw the HTML slip through.

bob_engineer: quick note: when json_mode=strict we currently enforce that upstream content-type is application/json and otherwise produce 422. that makes the client see invalid_json even when the real cause was upstream 500/html.

bob_engineer: short-term workaround for customers: either use json_mode=permissive or make Accept stronger so negotiation prefers json, e.g. "Accept: application/json;q=1.0, text/html;q=0.01". works around caches that favor html.

ergon_customer: worked for us with permissive. but we want a proper fix so our observability and error pages reflect upstream errors instead of 422.

carla_sre: we also observed some CDN caches rewrite or strip Accept q-values which can cause html wins. edge should be hardened so strict mode decisions don't rely on cache-modified Accept negotiation alone.

bob_engineer: proposed plan:
1) change mapping: when json_mode=strict and upstream returns content-type not json -> return structured 502 with fields {error: "upstream_non_json", upstream_status: <n>} instead of 422. keeps intent (client asked for strict json) but surfaces upstream failure class.
2) add metric strict_json.upstream_non_json and logs with request_id tag for 14d.
3) normalize content-type parsing (strip charset, accept prefixes) and relax reliance on cached Accept headers at edge.
4) docs + recommended Accept header example.

bob_engineer: i'll push a canary to staging with the 502 mapping + metric. if staging looks good i'll schedule a prod rollout during the next window.

deploy-bot: deploy request created by bob_engineer:canary -> eng-runtime/staging (id: deploy-8891). ETA ~12m.

alice_support: noted. i've linked this thread to ticket S-3429 and marked P2. leaving open until prod rollout.

ergon_customer: thanks all — permissive unblocked us but we'd prefer the 502 mapping. we'll test after you push.

bob_engineer: canary in progress. will post updates and any logs matching metric. thanks for the fast report. :thumbsup:
